editorial:
Imagine going back to a place where you once filmed a sad story and seeing how the real world actually looks compared to the movie version. That is exactly what happens here. You get to follow director Hirokazu Kore-eda and actress Makiko Esumi as they travel back to Wajima. It feels less like a formal documentary and more like a casual road trip with two old friends. They walk around the town, talk to the locals, and look at the landscapes that inspired their previous work. The vibe is very quiet and peaceful, making you feel like you are just tagging along for the ride on a rainy afternoon.

What really works is how honest the conversations feel. You will notice how the director focuses on small, everyday details rather than big drama. The pacing is slow, which might be a turn-off if you want action, but it is perfect for relaxing. If you enjoy seeing how movies are made, you will love this.
endingExplained: The film wraps up with a quiet reflection on memory and time. As the duo leaves Wajima, you see that the line between the fictional story they told and the real town has blurred. They realize that while the movie is finished, the real people and places keep changing. It ends not with a big twist, but with a soft feeling of closure and respect for the land they visited.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves slow cinema and behind the scenes looks at filmmaking.
